units.translation: first and in a primary sense we were declaring of a renowned army, that is, of a celebrated and trophy-bearing one, that is, through the army, in war we were renowned and directed, that is, they were led straight and extended, all the customs of the fortified and walled cities; and we were rushing according to the established customs against the cities being sacked, not sacking temples, not tearing up tombs, as Xerxes dared to do, and the customs that fortify and establish cities are also called pyrgina [tower-like].

Thus Hermann for φροντίσιν δαεὶς τὰν ἁ πυρδαή τινα πρόνοιαν [having been taught in thoughts the fire-consuming forethought]. Schol. οὕτω τὸ ἑξῆς, ἥντινα μήσατο πρόνοιαν τάλαινα Θεστιὰς ἡ παιδολυμὰς καὶ πυρδαής [thus the sequence: what forethought the wretched Thestias, child-destroying and fire-consuming, devised], who reads πυρδαής [fire-consuming].
Let him know who is not winged in his thoughts, that the child-destroying, wretched daughter of Thestius devised a fire-consuming forethought, burning the bloody age-mate of her son.

It was read πυριγενετᾶν [born in fire]. I restored πυριβρεμετᾶν [thundering with fire], which is hidden in the gloss of Timachidas of Rhodes excerpted by Hesychius, πυριβρεμέτας: ὁ χαλινός. Τιμαχίδας δέ· ἤτοι ὁ πυρὶ βρέμων, ἢ διὰ πυρὸς βρέμοντος γεγονώς [fire-thundering: the bridle. But Timachidas: either he who thunders with fire, or he who was born through thundering fire]. Where there is no reason why after χαλινός [bridle] some words added for the sake of interpretation should be thought to have fallen out.
